findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: DMARC record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy=none, pct=100, rua=true.

findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud, increasing phishing and payment-diversion risk during transaction communications; monitoring only provides no enforcement protection.

remediation.summary: Progress DMARC from p=none through quarantine to reject after validating all legitimate senders and DKIM/SPF alignment.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: SPF record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier=~all, lookup_count=2.

findings.deal_impact: Softfail weakens sender authentication and spoof resistance, supporting impersonation risk until hard fail is safely implemented.

remediation.summary: Inventory mail senders, validate SPF/DKIM alignment, then change ~all to -all with monitoring.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled

evidence.excerpt: DNSSEC enabled=false for DS query at brightwaterfleet.example.

findings.deal_impact: Un-signed DNS is more susceptible to spoofing/cache poisoning, though practical deal risk is lower than email and exposed-surface issues.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC with registrar/DNS provider, publish DS records, and test resolution and rollover procedures.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: Risky hostname pattern=vpn; first_seen=2023-02-11, last_seen=2026-09-30; risky_hostnames_count=4.

findings.deal_impact: Public names suggest VPN, legacy Jenkins, staging API and legacy portal attack surface that needs validation, hardening or decommissioning before close.

remediation.summary: Validate ownership and exposure of each risky hostname; restrict, patch, MFA-protect or decommission legacy/staging systems.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size

evidence.excerpt: CT query returned unique_hostnames=47, exceeding the rule threshold of 40 for a 201-1000 employee company.

findings.deal_impact: A 47-host certificate footprint suggests asset sprawl and possible unmanaged services, complicating inventory assurance and post-close attack-surface reduction.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames to owned business services, remove stale certificates/hosts, and implement certificate issuance approval.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support TLSv1.0=true, TLSv1.1=true, TLSv1.2=true; tls_versions=[TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2].

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www weakens transport security and may affect compliance/customer assurance; remediation is usually straightforward configuration work.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1, retain TLSv1.2+ with modern ciphers, and retest all hosted names.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: Security headers show strict-transport-security=null on the apex host.
Security headers show strict-transport-security=null on www host.

findings.deal_impact: Without HSTS, users may be more exposed to downgrade/SSL-stripping on first or insecure visits; low standalone deal risk.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security with appropriate max-age after confirming HTTPS across subdomains, then monitor.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: KEV match CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001 for ExampleGate SSL-VPN 7.0.11, match_tier=appliance_exposed, match_level=product; note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: This is a potential exposure only: an internet-facing appliance product appears in CISA KEV, but affected version was not verified. Confirm urgently because exploited VPN flaws can enable initial access.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify appliance version/firmware against CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, patch or isolate, rotate credentials, and review VPN logs for compromise.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. Entity match exact; disclosed_within_months=14.

findings.deal_impact: A disclosed incident 14 months ago raises diligence questions on root cause, notification/regulatory closure, remediation and cyber-insurability; may affect reps, indemnities and closing conditions.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident report, regulator correspondence, remediation evidence and insurance history; validate lessons learned and close any open actions.
